$comment: The architecture tests/library/rules/Composition.test.ts enforces. Paths are relative to packages/ui/src; stylesheets are relative to packages/ui/src/styles.

layers.$comment: Imports go down this list or stay in their layer. A module's layer is entries for the package's entry points, read from its exports, else its entry under modules, else for a module of a component's internal folder (<family>/internal/<component>/) that component's layer, else the longest matching entry under directories. A module of a family's folder that renders another component, or serves one that does, is listed as composites, and one of a composites folder that renders none as base, so a base control cannot import a composite; every other module takes its directory's layer. Any other module listed with a layer its directory doesn't give it takes { layer, reason }. Which modules may import a family's internal/ folder is ESLint's rule, in eslint.config.mjs.

icons/index.ts.reason: The generated index of every icon, beside the icons/* export.

foundations/ThemeToggle.tsx.reason: Its page is a foundation’s, and it renders IconButton.

foundations/ThemeMenuRadioGroup.tsx.reason: It sets the theme preference beside it, and renders Menu’s radio group.

internal/popup/PopupSurface.tsx.reason: It reads Theme and the skeleton.

layout/Layout.tsx.reason: Its page is in App frame & layout, but base controls such as Disclosure and Menubar lay out with it.

layout/Surface.tsx.reason: Its page is in App frame & layout, but Card and the dialogs’ parts build on it.

planned.$comment: Modules the rules above already name but that don't exist yet, so that work adding them in parallel needs no edit here. A planned module counts as present: it gives its directory a module and its component its stylesheet of the same name, and its component's classes may go unused until it exists. Once every planned module exists, empty this list.

interactive.$comment: Raw interactive HTML. An <input type="hidden"> and an element that is both aria-hidden and out of the tab order are not interactive. Widget roles count as interactive too; Tree and Calendar implement patterns no Base UI part covers, so they are the leaf controls for theirs.

dynamicRoles.$comment: The roles a role attribute the source doesn't spell out can take, per module and per expression by its source text, such as role={role}: the check counts each, so an interactive one needs a leaf-control entry above. A role={…} whose module and expression aren't listed here is a finding of its own.

classes.$comment: Every module is a component named after its file, except that a module of <family>/internal/<component>/ belongs to the component of <family>/<Component>.tsx. A component owns the classes that start with env-<file name in kebab case> and the stylesheet of the same name. An entry below adds classes (prefixes), stylesheets and other modules to a component; slots are classes another module may emit inside the component when it imports one of the component's modules. A class belongs to the component with the longest matching prefix. A stylesheet listed for a component holds that component's own rules, never rules that restyle another component.

shared.env-theme: The theme boundary, which every popup and provider sets.
shared.env-surface: The surface helper, which components render through Surface.
shared.env-connected-rows: The shared connected-row corners (ConnectedRows.css) of List.
shared.env-connected-row: The shared connected-row corners (ConnectedRows.css) of List.
shared.env-icon: The icon wrapper, which every component colors through currentColor and sizes through --env-icon-size.
shared.env-skeleton-content: A skeleton's inert content without a box, which every component that takes skeleton renders inside its busy root (Skeleton.css).
shared.env-skeleton-status: The visually hidden status beside a skeleton list (Skeleton.css).
shared.env-hover-detail: The dotted underline (HoverDetail.css) of text that shows more on hover or focus, which HoverCard and Tooltip give a text trigger.

stylesheetsWithoutComponent.Base.css: The layer order, the reset, the tokens, the theme boundary and the shared surface, icon and motion rules every component builds on.
stylesheetsWithoutComponent.Skeleton.css: The skeleton state every component that paints a container takes, by element and data-env-skeleton.
stylesheetsWithoutComponent.Reset.css: The margin of a themed document's body and the box-sizing reset inside every theme boundary.
stylesheetsWithoutComponent.HoverDetail.css: The dotted underline of text that shows more, which HoverCard and Tooltip give a text trigger.

childRules.$comment: A container may lay out a child that belongs to another component: place, size and space it, never restyle it. Each rule lets one stylesheet's selectors name a child's classes, as long as they declare only layoutProperties and the rule's own properties.

rules.note: A Page reckons the height of its sticky PageHeader from the rows the header has, read with :has(), so what scrolls into view in its content keeps clear of it; it never styles the header.

ButtonGroup joins its buttons into one control: it sizes them, squares their inner corners and insets their focus rings; where it holds buttons of mixed variants, read with :has(), it spaces them apart with their own corners instead.

The actions in the picker card's footer under a date, month or time, such as Today, Now and Clear, keep their labels on one line, so a row too narrow for them wraps whole buttons rather than the words inside one.
Under a coarse pointer, where there is often no keyboard, the palette leaves out the shortcut keys at the end of its items.
A code diff pads its loading state.
A leading icon button lines its icon up with the composer's inset.
A group reads with :has() whether its avatars show initials, which center in their circle, and then piles them looser and upright, setting only its own properties; it never styles the avatar.

An avatar in a combobox's leading slot takes the slot's size; the combobox reads with :has() whether it shows initials, and where the slot is too small for them leaves it out or closes the slot, setting only its own properties and layout; it never styles the avatar.
A task list item lines its checkbox up with the item's text.
Where the document scrolls, Panes in the body are as tall as their content, so a Scaffold lets the panes grow with the page rather than scroll; it never restyles them.

A Scaffold reads, with :has(), whether the top bar or the navigation form in a region of its own is on the page's background, the same as the body, and then draws a hairline on that region's edge toward the body; it never styles them.

A resizable side sheet makes its content, which scrolls with the sheet, at least as tall as the sheet and the containing block of its resize handle, so the handle runs down the whole edge; a side sheet's content fills its height and its actions sit at its foot. It never restyles them.

The picker card reads whether its body is a calendar alone, with :has(), to size itself, place the calendar and set the gap above its footer, and sizes a calendar alone to fill it: containing its inline size, so the card measures it at its seven days, and stretching it to the card's width; it never styles the calendar.
